text: Elfa watches the market. Over three point eight million A P I requests in August. Elfa decides when. It doesn't execute.

Elfa now tells users to run execution themselves. That runner is the dangerous piece: it double-fires on a retry, or acts on a forged request. And KeeperHub's webhook needs a bearer header Elfa can't send.
So the bridge sits between them. A Cloudflare Worker proves who sent the event, proves it isn't a repeat, and forwards it once.

The KeeperHub workflow is where every number lives. Balance check, live Uniswap quote, price floor, then a fixed swap of zero point zero zero two Eth into U S D C on Base. The webhook can't change any of it.

The live Worker, hit with signed harness events. The first one forwards. The same event again is dropped as a duplicate. A forged signature is refused and never written. Every decision lands in a public audit log.
The proof run, launched directly on KeeperHub. Seven steps, all green. Zero point zero zero two Eth became four point nine two U S D C. KeeperHub sponsored the gas. The receipt is on BaseScan.
A later run found under a thousandth of an Eth in the wallet, below the guard. It stopped before the quote, moved nothing, and still told the operator why.
One honest note. Only one real Elfa event has reached the bridge so far, an expiry notice, and the Worker dropped it. One hundred sixty six tests pin every money value.
Elfa decides when. KeeperHub decides how much.
